name: No-minimum micro-volume FBA prep for small Amazon sellers
buyer: Small US Amazon sellers moving a few hundred units a month who are below prep-center minimums
pain: Amazon ended its in-house FBA prep service in January 2026, so sellers must label, polybag and package themselves. Prep errors that cost cents can now cost several dollars.
wedge: Offer no monthly minimum and a flat per-unit price for label plus bag. A seller at 300 units a month pays an effective $0.67-$1.67 per unit at the cited minimums, which is simple division.

scan1Edge.entrant_basis: The entrant sells pay-per-unit with no monthly minimum, at a flat $0.60-$0.80 (estimate). It needs a thermal label printer, poly bags, a scale and shelving, and no licences.
scan1Edge.falsifier: If existing prep shops already offer no-minimum small-seller plans, or the entrant can't process units fast enough to profit at the flat price, the edge fails.

unitEconomicsNoted.notes: The $0.60-$0.80 flat price and the 35-55% margin are the notes' own estimates and depend on throughput near 100 units an hour. Labor, materials and insurance are not itemized.

majorUncertainty: Whether the entrant can process units fast enough, earn seller trust without reviews, and stay within the 20-hour weekly limit.
unknowns: Conflicting defect-fee figures ($0.32-$1.74 versus $0.32-$5.72 per unit) were not resolved
Direct seller complaints about minimums were not found
Throughput per hour is an estimate
Whether some prep shops already offer no-minimum plans
regulatoryOrPlatformDependency: Depends on Amazon inbound and labeling rules. Needs a US address that can receive cartons and inventory insurance. Home operation may hit zoning limits.
